title: High-purity entanglement mediated by magnons despite weak coupling
abstract: Entangling distant spins via a shared magnonic bus typically faces a tradeoff: stronger spin-magnon coupling increases the entanglement fidelity, but also the spin decay rate. We propose a protocol that breaks this tradeoff. The magnons couple only to a transition outside the computational basis, in which the Bell state is created. Our protocol is probabilistic, and weak coupling reduces the success probability but not the fidelity. We analyze a setup where the spins are two nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near a magnetic wire. In the absence of NV dephasing, the protocol reaches unit fidelity with a maximally entangled state, for arbitrarily weak coupling. In our simulations via the Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach, the NV-magnon coupling is taken to be one-third of the magnon linewidth. Considering finite NV dephasing, we predict a fidelity of >0.99 for a state-of-the-art rate, and an optimal fidelity of 0.91 for a moderate rate, both at 0.6% success probability.
summary: The paper presents a novel probabilistic protocol to generate high-fidelity entanglement between distant NV centers using magnons as a quantum bus. It successfully breaks the conventional trade-off between coupling strength and decoherence by engineering the interaction such that only transitions outside the computational basis are coupled to the magnon bath. The results show near-unity fidelity is achievable even with weak coupling, making it highly relevant for solid-state quantum networking.
main_problem: The research aims to overcome a fundamental trade-off in quantum entanglement generation where increasing spin-magnon coupling enhances fidelity but simultaneously increases the decoherence rate.
main_result: A probabilistic protocol was proposed that achieves high entanglement fidelity, even with arbitrarily weak coupling, by utilizing magnon measurement to protect the computational subspace from decay.
method: The analysis uses a Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach (stochastic unravelling) applied to the system's master equation dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical platform involves two Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers coupled via magnons propagating in a thin magnetic wire. The protocol relies on coupling magnons only to transitions outside the computational basis to preserve coherence.

paper_structure: The paper first identifies the entanglement trade-off, then proposes a probabilistic protocol based on magnon measurement to circumvent this limit. It details the Hamiltonian and dynamics using MC wavefunction simulations, culminating in quantitative predictions of achievable fidelity under realistic decoherence conditions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses scalable quantum networking by demonstrating how solid-state spin systems can mediate entanglement robustly against coupling strength limitations, a key challenge in quantum information science.
